summary: Checks whether a value is **not** an HtmlOutput.
description: `nonHtmlOutput(value)` is the same test as `!isHtmlOutput(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard looks for the methods that define the type — `getContent`, `setTitle`, `setXFrameOptionsMode`. A stub that implements them passes, which is what makes code using this guard testable outside the runtime.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not an HtmlOutput; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript const output = HtmlService.createHtmlOutput("

hi

"); nonHtmlOutput({}); // => true nonHtmlOutput(null); // => true nonHtmlOutput(output); // => false ```
